about.what: Three rule-based macro 'regime' lenses, computed by code (not the AI): a Growth × Inflation momentum quadrant (Investment-Clock style), Growth × Policy, and Credit × Duration.
about.why: Asset classes have historically behaved differently depending on whether growth and inflation are accelerating or decelerating, whether policy is tight or loose, and whether credit or duration is leading.
about.how_to_read: Growth × Inflation shows the DIRECTION of change, not the level. Growth score = average of (1) the 6-month change in industrial production YoY (±2pp = ±1); (2) initial claims, 4-week average vs 26-week average, inverted (a 4-week average 10% above the 26-week average = −1; a sustained 10% jump in claims ≈ −0.83 because the 26-week average includes the recent weeks); (3) the 2-quarter change in real GDP YoY (±1pp = ±1). Inflation score = average 6-month change in core CPI YoY and core PCE YoY (±1pp = ±1). Each axis is accelerating at ≥ +0.1, decelerating at ≤ −0.1, otherwise flat (shown as a boundary between two quadrants). Quadrants: Goldilocks (growth up, inflation down), Inflationary boom (both up), Stagflation (growth down, inflation up), Disinflationary slowdown (both down). Growth × Policy: real policy rate = Fed funds target-range midpoint − core PCE YoY; above 1% restrictive, below 0.5% accommodative, otherwise neutral (within 0.15pp of an edge is borderline; r* itself is uncertain). Credit × Duration: 3-month total return of HYG minus IEI and LQD minus IEF (duration-matched); above +0.5pp credit leads, below −0.5pp duration leads, otherwise balanced, with the 3-month change in the high-yield spread as a cross-check. Inputs older than their release cycle are dropped and listed. Historical tendencies are code-written generalisations from the Investment Clock study, not forecasts; the AI only explains.

growth_inflation.label: Goldilocks / Inflationary boom boundary
growth_inflation.level_note: Quadrants describe the direction of change, not the level: core PCE inflation is still 3.1% vs the 2% target.

growth_policy.label: Neutral policy, growth rising
growth_policy.note: r* (the neutral real rate) is uncertain: FOMC longer-run projections imply about 1%, Holston-Laubach-Williams estimates range about 0.7–1.3%.

items.text: Equities have historically tended to outperform bonds, commodities and cash in this phase.
Cyclical and growth sectors have historically tended to lead defensive sectors.
Commodities have historically tended to lag as inflation cools.

tendencies.basis: Greetham & Hartnett (2004), 'The Investment Clock', Merrill Lynch: average US asset-class and sector returns by growth/inflation phase, 1973–2004. Averages hide wide variation; past patterns are not forecasts.
